newsitem.title: USA: CBOT soybeans fall limit as USDA hikes production.
newsitem.headline: CBOT soybeans fall limit as USDA hikes production.

text.p: CBOT soybean futures skidded the 30-cent-per-bushel trading limit in nearly every contract by the close, with a hike by USDA in its outlook for 1996 U.S. soybean production the catalyst for the slide, traders said.
"The numbers set the tone for the market today and beans are acting like they should. There are too many beans," said Steve Bruce of E.D. and F. Man International.

Fund selling was estimated at least 35 million bushels, traders said. A selling pool of roughly six million bushels was noted at the close and options synthetics indicated a 10 cent per bushel lower open Monday, they said.
Soybeans Monday will trade with expanded 45-cent limits.

USDA early Friday said 1996 U.S. soybean production would total 2.346 billion bushels, up from an average trade estimate for 2.287 billion and above the government's forecast in September for 2.270 billion bushels.

USDA also increased to 195 million bushels its forecast for U.S. 1996-97 U.S. ending stocks of soybeans from the September outlook for 160 million bushels. The 1996-97 marketing year ends on August 31, 1997.
Soybeans closed 19-1/4 to 30 cents per bushel lower, with November down 30 at $7.00-1/4 per bushel.

Key sellers included Refco Inc with 12.0 million sold in November and five million in January, traders said. Smith Barney sold five million November, Prudential Securities sold three million November and Iowa Grain sold two million November and sold two million January, traders said.

Technicians said sell stops were triggered on the open when November broke below chart support at roughly $7.20 per bushel which was considered a support level because it was near a low for the recent move.
The nine day relative strength index (RSI) for November closed at 16.917 points, down from the 20 area which is generally considered a very oversold level.
Soybean futures volume was estimated at 75,000 contracts, up from 54,136 Thursday, according to the CBOT.

Soybean options activity featured Rosenthal Collins' purchase of 2,000 November $7.00 puts at 7-1/2 to 14 cents, Smith Barney bought 3,000 January $7.25 puts and sold 3,000 January $7.00 puts at 14 to 14-1/2 cents, traders said. Smith Barney also bought 1,500 March $7.25 puts and sold 1,500 March $7.00 puts at 14 cents, traders said.
Soybean options volume was estimated at 35,000 contracts, up from 26,093 Thursday.
